## section: pipeline
    Ingestion > Pipeline
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/ingestion#pipeline
## Pipeline {#pipeline}

`Pipeline` is the main entry point. It handles file loading, extraction, chunking, embedding, and indexing. It supports batch processing with concurrency, progress tracking, and checkpointing.

```python
from mistralai.search.toolkit.ingestion.pipelines import Pipeline
from mistralai.client import Mistral
from mistralai.search.toolkit.embedding import MistralEmbedder, MODEL_1024_EMBEDDING
from mistralai.search.toolkit.ingestion.extractors import PlainTextExtractor
from mistralai.search.toolkit.ingestion.loaders import FilesystemFileLoader
from mistralai.search.toolkit.ingestion.text_splitters import CharacterTextSplitter
from mistralai.search.toolkit.ingestion.enrichment import SummaryEnricher
from mistralai.search.toolkit.llm import MistralChat, LLMConfig
from mistralai.search.toolkit.plugins.vespa import VespaClientConfig
from vespa_app import app

mistral_client = Mistral(api_key="...")
llm = MistralChat(client=mistral_client, config=LLMConfig(model="mistral-small-latest"))

collection_name = "my_collection"
config = VespaClientConfig(
    endpoint="http://localhost:8080",
)

vector_store = app.get_search_index(config, collection_name=collection_name)

pipeline = Pipeline(
    loader=FilesystemFileLoader(),
    extractor=PlainTextExtractor(),
    text_splitter=CharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=512),
    processors=[SummaryEnricher(llm_provider=llm)],
    embedder=MistralEmbedder(client=mistral_client, model_name=MODEL_1024_EMBEDDING),
    stores=vector_store,
)

num_chunks = await pipeline.run(documents=["doc1.txt", "doc2.txt"])
```

> **Info**
>
> `collection_name` (passed to `app.get_search_index`) selects which schema/collection your chunks are indexed into. Use the same name when retrieving documents later.

page: https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/ingestion | "Ingestion" | section: ingestion

## section: ingestion
    Ingestion
    cite: https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/search/search-toolkit/ingestion
# Ingestion

Ingestion transforms raw documents into searchable chunks indexed in a vector store. You can swap pipeline components based on your needs.

A `FileLoader` reads raw bytes from a source (local filesystem, cloud storage, or any custom source) and returns a `File` object.

A `DocumentExtractor` converts that `File` into a structured `Document` by parsing PDFs via OCR, converting HTML to Markdown, or reading plain text depending on the file type.

A `TextSplitter` divides the `Document` into smaller `DocumentChunk` objects. The strategy and chunk size directly affect retrieval quality.

Optional `DocumentProcessor` stages (such as a `ChunkEnricher` or `SummaryEnricher`) add metadata to each chunk before indexing, for example an LLM-generated summary or entity tags.

An `Embedder` converts each chunk into a vector, and the store persists both the vector and the raw text for search.

The stages of an ingestion `Pipeline` are:
- `FileLoader`
- `DocumentExtractor`
- `TextSplitter`
- `Embedder`
- `store`

The only optional stage is `DocumentProcessor` (passed as `processors`).

**Required parameters for `Pipeline`**: `loader`, `extractor`, `text_splitter`, `embedder`, and `stores`.
If your code raises a `TypeError` about a missing argument, you are likely omitting one of these five required arguments.
